Disposal, With All Statutory Benefits.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Heard Sri.S.S.Sajjanshetty, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri.G.B.Yadav, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondents.
2. The appellant was the owner of land bearing Sy.No.50/2 measuring 6 acres 20 guntas situated at Sangolgi- G village, Tq: Aland, Dist: Kalaburagi, which was acquired for the purpose of "Amarja Project" vide preliminary notification under Section 4(1) of L.A.Act, dated 09.07.1992.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation of Rs.8,000/- per acre for dry land based on sales statistics method followed by common award dated 29.08.1996.

The appellant has filed protest petition seeking reference within limitation for higher NC: 2024:KHC-K:2198 award based on capitalization method taking two crops and the said reference under Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was registered in LAC No.358/2003 on the file of the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn)
Aland, which is allowed by judgment and award dated 12.01.2005 by determining the market value at Rs.32,750/- per acre for dry land with statutory benefits and interest.
Dissatisfied with the said determination, the appellant has filed appeal in LACA No.685/2012 with an application for condonation of delay of 2749 days.

The said appeal was allowed by the judgment and award dated 03.01.2017 by enhancing Rs.95,040/- per acre from Rs.32,750/- per acre, which is the subject matter of this appeal seeking further enhancement restricted claim at Rs.1,50,000/- per acre of dry land.
On these grounds sought for allowing of the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader submits that the compensation awarded by the First Appellate Court is just and proper and there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award.
However, he fairly submits that the respondents have not challenged the award dated 20.04.2018 on the file of the III Addl. District Judge, Kalaburagi.

sentences.text:
2 4. It is not in dispute that the land involved in this case are acquired under the same notification,
same village and for the same purpose.

The First Appellate Court has awarded the compensation of Rs.95,040/- per acre by relying on the judgment of this Court in MSA No.757/2012 in the case of Ambaraya S/o: Basanna Vs. Special Land Acquisition Officer, M and MIP, Gulbarga, wherein the compensation has been enhanced to Rs.95,040/- per acre from Rss.32,750/- per acre.

entities.text: Basanna Vs. Special Land Acquisition Officer, M and MIP, Gulbarga
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the appeal in MSA No.848/2012 reveals that the First Appellate Court has dismissed LACA No.14/2010.

Being aggrieved by the said judgment the appellants/Baburao and another have preferred appeal in MSA No.848/2012 which came to be allowed vide order dated 24.10.2017 and the matter was remitted to the First Appellate Court for disposal in accordance with law.
Accordingly, the First Appellate Court has passed the award by determining the market value @ Rs.1,85,229/- per acre with all statutory benefits.

It is also not in dispute the respondents have not challenged this judgment and award passed by the First Appellate Court vide order dated 20.04.2018 and the award amount is also satisfied.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:2198 5.

For the aforesaid reasons and discussions and keeping in mind the principle of parity, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part with costs.

(b) The appellant in this appeal is also entitled for the compensation of Rs.1,85,229/-
per acre in respect of land bearing Sy.No.50/2 of Sangolgi-C village, Tq: Aland, Dist:
Kalaburagi, with all statutory benefits with costs.
However, the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period before this Court as well as First Appellate Court.
(c) Six weeks time is granted to pay the deficit Court fee.
